tools.name: proof_fetch_preflight
tools.description: Free: checks a public URL and returns fetchability, provenance, hashes, deterministic injection indicators and a free preview of the first 1,000 or so characters of text (short pages come back whole); not a safety guarantee. No payment or purchase. Example: {"url":"https://example.com/","maxChars":3

tools.name: proof_fetch_offer
tools.description: Returns the offer and request schema without buying. Full cited text: 1,000 free extractions with a free key (no card), then $0.01 a page either way: a 500-page card pack for $5, or $0.50 per Stripe MPP call, which returns the page plus an API key holding 49 more. tools.description: Fetch a public URL and return its cited, paragraph-addressable text with integrity hashes and a receipt. Uses one credit from a ProofFetch key, and only when extraction succeeds. findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "proof_fetch_evidence" references sensitive artifacts (authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: proof_fetch_preflight, proof_fetch_offer, proof_fetch_evidence · Private data: proof_fetch_offer · Public sink: proof_fetch_offer, proof_fetch_evidence.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: proof_fetch_preflight, proof_fetch_offer, proof_fetch_evidence · Private data: proof_fetch_offer · Public sink: proof_fetch_offer, proof_fetch_evidence

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
